runs.text: Tail bounds control the probability that a random variable lies far from a threshold or its mean.
Chebyshev follows by applying Markov to the nonnegative variable (X-mu)^2. The union bound needs no independence.

items.text: Markov requires a nonnegative random variable, a positive threshold, and a finite expectation for a finite bound.
Chebyshev requires a finite mean and variance and a positive deviation
These bounds are distribution-free and can be loose; a value above 1 may be replaced by the trivial bound 1.

examples.title: Bound a deviation from the mean

items.text: Do not apply Markov directly to a variable that can be negative.
The union bound is an upper bound, not generally an equality.
